title: Talking and Working Online
tagline: Email, messaging and video calls for daily life and work.
description: Email, WhatsApp and video calls connect you with family, schools, employers and services. This course takes you from making your first email address to joining an online meeting with confidence, and shows you how to communicate clearly and politely.
outcomes: Create and use an email address
Send photos and documents as attachments
Use WhatsApp messages and voice notes well
Make and join video calls and online meetings

modules.title: Email
modules.summary: Your own address, clear messages and attachments.

lessons.title: Create your email address
lessons.body:
An **email address** is like a postal address for the internet. Employers, schools, banks and government services often ask for one. It is also needed for the Play Store and many apps.

An email address looks like this: **mutale.banda@gmail.com**. The part before the @ is your name. The part after is the email service.

## Making a Gmail address
Gmail is free and works well on phones.

1. Open the **Gmail** app (on Android it is already installed) or go to gmail.com.
2. Tap **Create account**, then **For my personal use**.
3. Type your first and last name.
4. Type your date of birth.
5. Choose your address. Gmail will suggest some, or you can type your own.
6. Create a strong **password**: a long sentence only you know.
7. Add your **phone number**. This helps you get back in if you forget your password.

## Choosing a good address
For work and school, use your real name: **mutale.banda** or **mbanda1990**. Avoid playful names like *coolboy_zed*. An employer will see your address before they meet you.

## Write it down safely
Write your email address on paper you keep at home, so you can share it correctly. Keep your password separate and private.

## Check your inbox
Open Gmail once a day. Important messages from employers or schools may come by email, not SMS.
key_points: An email address looks like name@gmail.com
Use your real name for work and school
Add your phone number so you can recover it
lessons.try_it: If you do not have an email address yet, create one now.

lessons.title: Writing a clear, polite email
lessons.body:
A good email is short, clear and polite. It helps people understand what you need and answer quickly.

## The parts of an email
- **To:** the email address of the person you are writing to. Check every letter.
- **Subject:** a few words saying what the email is about, like *Application for shop assistant job*. Never leave it empty.
- **Message:** what you want to say.

## A simple shape
1. **Greeting:** *Dear Mrs Phiri,* or *Good morning,*
2. **Who you are**, in one line: *My name is Mutale Banda from Chipata.*
3. **Why you are writing**, in one or two lines: *I would like to apply for the shop assistant job I saw at the market.*
4. **What happens next:** *My CV is attached. I am available for an interview any weekday.*
5. **Closing:** *Thank you. Kind regards, Mutale Banda, 097...*

## Tips
- Keep it short. Three or four short paragraphs are enough.
- Do not write in CAPITAL LETTERS. It looks like shouting.
- Read it once before you send. Check names, numbers and spelling.
- Reply within a day or two to important emails.

## Cc and Bcc
**Cc** sends a copy to someone else so they know about it. **Bcc** sends a hidden copy. When emailing many people who do not know each other, use Bcc so their addresses stay private.
key_points: Always write a clear subject
Greeting, who you are, why you write, closing
Read it once before you send
lessons.try_it: Write a short email to a friend or family member with a clear subject line.

lessons.title: Sending photos and documents
lessons.body:
An **attachment** is a file sent with an email or a message, like a photo, a CV or a form.

## Attaching a file in Gmail
1. Start a new email and fill in To and Subject.
2. Tap the **paper clip** icon at the top.
3. Choose the file from your phone, or a photo from your gallery.
4. Wait until the file appears in the email, then tap **Send**.

## Taking a clear photo of a document
Often you need to send a picture of a certificate, a form or a letter.

- Put the paper on a flat, dark surface in good light, near a window.
- Hold the phone straight above the paper, not at an angle.
- Make sure all four corners are in the picture and nothing is blurred.

Better still, use **scan**: in the Google Drive app, tap **+**, then **Scan**. It straightens the page and saves it as a **PDF**, the format most offices prefer.

## Name your files
Name your CV *Mutale_Banda_CV.pdf*, not *IMG_2041.jpg*. It looks professional and is easy to find.

## Size
Very large files, like long videos, may not send by email. Email usually allows about 25 MB. For bigger files, share a link from Google Drive instead.

## Be careful with attachments you receive
Only open attachments from people you know and expect. Unexpected files, especially ones ending in .apk or .exe, can harm your phone.
key_points: Tap the paper clip to attach a file
Scan documents to PDF with Google Drive
Only open attachments you expect
lessons.try_it: Use Google Drive's Scan to make a PDF of any page at home.

modules.title: Messaging and calls
modules.summary: WhatsApp, voice notes, video calls and group manners.

lessons.title: WhatsApp messages and voice notes
lessons.body:
**WhatsApp** sends messages, photos, voice notes and calls using data or Wi-Fi instead of airtime.

## Sending a message
1. Open WhatsApp and tap the **chat** button.
2. Choose a contact. They must be saved in your phone and have WhatsApp.
3. Type your message in the box at the bottom and tap the **send** arrow.

## What the ticks mean
- **One grey tick:** sent from your phone.
- **Two grey ticks:** delivered to their phone.
- **Two blue ticks:** they have read it.

## Voice notes
Voice notes are useful if typing is hard. **Press and hold** the microphone button, speak, then let go to send. Slide your finger to the bin to cancel. Speak clearly and keep it short: under one minute is best. Long voice notes use more data and many people will not listen to them.

## Sending photos and documents
Tap the **paper clip** or **camera** in the chat. To send a document such as a PDF, choose **Document**. Documents keep their full quality.

## Being polite
- Greet first, as you would in person: *Good morning, Sir.*
- For work or officials, send messages in working hours unless it is urgent.
- Do not send many messages one after another. Put your request in one clear message.

## Deleting a message
Press and hold a message, then tap the bin. Choose **Delete for everyone** if you sent it by mistake. The other person will see that a message was deleted.
key_points: Two blue ticks mean the message was read
Keep voice notes short
Greet first and keep requests clear
lessons.try_it: Send a short voice note to a family member.

lessons.title: Making a video call
lessons.body:
A **video call** lets you see and talk to someone at the same time. It is great for family far away, and for interviews and meetings.

## Video call on WhatsApp
1. Open the chat with the person.
2. Tap the **video camera** icon at the top.
3. When they answer, you will see each other.
4. Tap the red button to end the call.

To call a group, open a group chat and tap the video icon, then choose who to call.

## Before an important call
- **Charge your phone** or keep it plugged in.
- Check your **data**: video calls use a lot. A 10-minute video call can use around 50 to 100 MB. Use Wi-Fi if you can.
- Find a **quiet place** with light in front of your face, not behind you.
- Rest the phone on something steady at eye level, so your face is not shaking.

## During the call
- Look at the camera when you speak, not only at the screen.
- If the picture freezes, turn your video off and continue with voice only. It uses much less data.
- Tap the **microphone** to mute yourself when others are talking in a group call and there is noise around you.

## If the call keeps dropping
Move closer to a window or outside for a better signal, or switch between mobile data and Wi-Fi.
key_points: Tap the video camera icon in a chat
Charge your phone and check data first
Turn video off to save data if the picture freezes
lessons.try_it: Make a short video call to someone you know.

lessons.title: Group chat manners
lessons.body:
WhatsApp groups bring together family, churches, schools, savings groups and workplaces. Good manners keep them useful and friendly.

## Before you post
- Is it **for the whole group**, or just one person? Reply privately when it is personal: press and hold their message, tap the three dots, and choose **Reply privately**.
- Is it **true**? Check before forwarding news and warnings.
- Is it on topic? A work group is not the place for jokes and chain messages.

## Good habits
- Keep messages short and clear.
- **Reply to a specific message** by swiping right on it, so others know what you are answering.
- Do not send many good-morning pictures or videos. They use everyone's data and space.
- Respect quiet hours, especially in work and school groups.
- Never share other people's photos or phone numbers without asking.

## If you run a group
As an **admin**, you can:

- Set the group so **only admins can send messages** for announcements.
- Write a short group description with the rules.
- Remove people who post scams or insults.

## Mute instead of leaving
If a group is too busy, you can **mute** it: open the group, tap its name, then **Mute notifications**. You stay in the group without your phone ringing all day.

## Disagreeing politely
It is fine to disagree. Talk about the idea, not the person, and take long arguments to a private chat.
key_points: Reply privately when it is personal
Check before forwarding news
Mute busy groups instead of leaving
lessons.try_it: Mute one very busy group on your phone.

modules.title: Working online
modules.summary: Online meetings, sharing files and a professional presence.

lessons.title: Joining an online meeting
lessons.body:
Many workshops, interviews and trainings now happen online, using apps like **Google Meet**, **Zoom** or **Microsoft Teams**. You usually join by tapping a **link**.

## Before the meeting
- You receive a link by email or WhatsApp, with the date and time. Check the time zone if it is from another country.
- Install the app the meeting uses from the Play Store a day before. Some links also open in your web browser.
- Charge your phone and check your data or Wi-Fi. One hour of video can use a lot of data.

## Joining
1. Tap the link a few minutes early.
2. Type your **real name** when asked, so the organiser knows who you are.
3. Allow the app to use your camera and microphone if it asks.
4. Tap **Join**. You may wait in a "waiting room" until the host lets you in.

## The main buttons
- **Microphone:** tap to mute and unmute. Stay muted when you are not speaking.
- **Camera:** turn video on or off.
- **Chat:** type a question without interrupting.
- **Raise hand:** asks to speak politely.
- **Leave:** the red button ends the meeting for you.

## Good habits
- Say your name before you speak in a large meeting.
- If your connection is weak, turn your camera off and keep listening.
- Write down important dates and tasks during the meeting.
key_points: Join a few minutes early with your real name
Stay muted when you are not speaking
Use the chat or raise hand to ask questions
lessons.try_it: Install Google Meet or Zoom so you are ready for your next meeting.

lessons.title: Sharing and keeping documents online
lessons.body:
Saving important documents online keeps them safe if your phone is lost, and makes them easy to share.

## Google Drive
Every Gmail account comes with free storage in **Google Drive**. You can keep your CV, certificates and photos of important documents there.

## Uploading a file
1. Open the **Drive** app.
2. Tap **+**, then **Upload**.
3. Choose the file from your phone.

Now you can open it from any phone or computer by signing in to your Gmail account.

## Sharing a file with a link
1. In Drive, tap the three dots next to the file.
2. Tap **Share**, or **Copy link**.
3. Choose who can see it: only the people you add, or anyone with the link.
4. Paste the link in an email or WhatsApp message.

Sharing a link is better than sending a big file, because it uses less data.

## Folders
Make folders such as *CV and certificates*, *School*, and *Business*. Then you can find things quickly.

## Keep sensitive documents private
Be careful with documents showing your NRC, bank details or medical information. Do not share them with **anyone with the link**. Share only with the specific person who needs them, and remove access when they are done.

## Free space is limited
The free storage is large but not unlimited. Delete old copies and large videos you no longer need.
key_points: Keep important documents in Google Drive
Share a link instead of a big file
Share sensitive files only with specific people
lessons.try_it: Upload your CV or one important document to Google Drive.

lessons.title: Being professional online
lessons.body:
How you communicate online shapes how employers, customers and officials see you. Small habits make a big difference.

## Your profile
- Use a clear **profile picture** of your face on WhatsApp and email. It helps people recognise you.
- Write a short, simple **About**, such as *Tailor, Kitwe* or *Available for work*.
- Use your real name.

## Responding
- Reply to work messages within a day, even if only to say *Received, I will get back to you on Friday.*
- If you cannot make a meeting or deadline, say so early and politely.
- Thank people when they help you.

## Writing well
- Use full sentences, not text-speak like *pls hw r u*.
- Check names and numbers before sending.
- Be polite even when you are unhappy. Stay calm and stick to the facts.

## Your online footprint
Employers sometimes look at Facebook and other public profiles. Before you post, think: would I be comfortable if an employer saw this? You can set your posts to **Friends only** to keep personal life separate.

## Separate work and personal
If you use your phone for business, consider a separate **WhatsApp Business** account. It lets you set a business profile, working hours and quick replies, and keeps work messages apart from family chats.
key_points: Use a clear photo and your real name
Reply to work messages within a day
Think about who can see your posts
lessons.try_it: Update your WhatsApp profile photo and About to look clear and professional.

quiz.question: What is the best Subject for a job application email?
quiz.explanation: A clear subject tells the reader what the email is about.

quiz.question: You join an online meeting but there is noise around you. What should you do?
options: Mute your microphone when you are not speaking
quiz.explanation: Muting keeps the meeting clear for everyone.

quiz.question: What is the best way to send a large file to someone?
options: Read it out on a call
quiz.explanation: A link uses less data and works for big files.

quiz.question: Who should you share a file showing your NRC with?
options: Only the specific person who needs it
quiz.explanation: Sensitive documents should only go to people who really need them.

quiz.question: You cannot meet a work deadline. What is professional?
options: Send a voice note at midnight
quiz.explanation: Telling people early shows respect and builds trust.
